title: Home sleep apnea test
what: You take a small device home and sleep with it for one night. It records your breathing, oxygen, and pulse.
why: For loud snoring, pauses in breathing during sleep, and strong daytime sleepiness.
duration: one night at home; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: If you take sleeping pills or sedatives
If you have heart or lung conditions

prepare.title: Evening
prepare.text: No alcohol or sleeping pills, unless your doctor allowed them. Go to bed at your usual time.

prepare.title: Fingers
prepare.text: Remove polish from the nail where the sensor will go.

prepare.title: The device
prepare.text: The nurse will show you how to put on the sensors. Ask to write it down or take photos.

bring: A bag to return the device
steps: At the clinic, you are shown the device and how to put it on
In the evening before bed, you put a belt with sensors around your chest
A thin tube goes under your nose, and an oxygen sensor on your finger
You turn on the device and sleep as usual
In the morning, you take off the sensors and turn off the device
You return the device to the clinic the same day
feel: The first few minutes feel strange, but most people fall asleep fine
The tube under your nose may bother you
after: Reading the results usually takes a few days
Take the results to your doctor. They will explain them and suggest treatment
If a sensor came off at night, say so when you return the device

faq.a: A few hours of sleep is usually enough. If there is too little recording, the test may be repeated.

faq.q: How is this different from a sleep lab?
faq.a: At home there are fewer sensors and you sleep in your own bed. For some people, the doctor will still order a sleep lab study.

reminders.text: Sleep test tonight. No alcohol this evening. Put on the sensors as you were shown and turn on the device.
